welcome_body: Read your own documents and ask about the passages that matter. Your library stays on this computer.
connect: Use your Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity login
connect_body: CLI providers start disabled. Enable one here to use its login. Discovery and chat may contact provider services and CLI telemetry endpoints. Chat sends questions, conversation history, document metadata and selected text to your chosen provider. You can read without connecting. Without a selection, the document outline and opening excerpt are sent. Earlier selections can remain in conversation history.
signin: Not ready yet? Install the CLI and sign in in Terminal, then check again.
key_saved: Key saved. The connection has not been tested.
bring: Start with something you care about
bring_body: Add your notes, a paper, or a short sample. Your original file is kept alongside a readable copy. The first conversion asks to download packages from PyPI and possibly Python from GitHub. Choose Offline to read Markdown and text; retry conversion when ready.
sample_added: Your sample is in the Library.
coach: Three small ways to go further
coach_body: No setup to perfect. Start with one question.
tip_select: Select a passage, then ask why it matters or request an example.
tip_pin: Pin what you return to. Use folders to give each topic a home.
tip_usage: Keep an eye on Usage. Set a monthly budget at your own pace.
name: Your name (optional)
preview_passage: Reading becomes understanding when we connect new ideas.
preview_question: How does this help me learn?
preview_answer: Link a new concept to something you already know.
setup_help: AI comes from another service. Reading files is free of AI charges. To ask AI, first set up an account with OpenAI or Anthropic. An API key is a secret code from that account; API use can cost extra, even with a chat subscription. CLI means a separate app that you install and sign in to before refreshing this list. You can skip this and read a sample now.
step_welcome: Your coursework, with a way forward
step_welcome_body: Bring school deadlines and your reading into one place. Open a document, understand a passage, and check what to do next.
step_language_body: This changes the buttons and instructions. Your documents keep their original language. Change this later in Settings.
step_appearance_body: Choose a theme pack and System, Light, or Dark. These are the same controls as Settings, and you can change them later.
step_goal: What would you like to do first?
step_goal_body: Choose one starting point. You can use all three later.
goal_school_body: See courses, due work, and announcements. You will need your school’s sign-in.
goal_documents_body: Read lecture notes, papers, or study materials stored on this computer.
goal_sample_body: No school account, downloads, or AI key needed.
step_ai_body: You can read and organise files without AI. Connect a service only when you want to ask a question.
ai_free: What works without paying for AI
ai_free_body: Read the sample, import Markdown or text, organise your library, and view connected school coursework.
ai_paid: An API key is a secret code for an AI account
ai_paid_body: OpenAI or Anthropic can charge for questions sent with a key. A ChatGPT or Claude chat subscription does not automatically include API use.
ai_login: Already use Claude Code, Codex, or Antigravity?
ai_login_body: Their command-line apps use a separate sign-in in Terminal. Enable one in Settings after signing in. Its plan limits and fees still apply. Nothing is enabled here.
ai_privacy_body: An enabled provider receives your question, chat history, document details, and selected text. Without a selection, it receives an outline and opening excerpt. Earlier selections can remain in history. Enabled command-line apps may also contact their own services. VStudy sends no analytics.
ai_keychain_body: Saving or unlocking a key may ask for macOS Keychain access. Settings also offers “Use without saving keys” for this session only. Skip setup to avoid these prompts.
step_start_body: Follow the instructions below. Help is always available at the top of the app.
before_school: Choose Connect my school below. Search by school name, country, or Moodle URL. Selecting a result or checking a URL contacts that site and may download its logo. Sign in only after confirming the site. Protecting your school sign-in may ask for macOS Keychain access. Never paste your school password into AI chat.
before_documents: Choose a file below. It is copied into your local library. PDF and Office conversion asks before downloading tools from PyPI and possibly Python from GitHub. Choose Offline to use Markdown or text without downloads. Scanned PDFs have no readable text here.
before_sample: Add the sample, then open it. Read first. To practice asking about a passage, select a sentence and choose Ask about this. Sending a question needs an AI connection; the walkthrough itself is offline.
offline_promise: No school connection or AI is started by this guide. You can leave now and resume from Home or Help.
save_error: Could not save progress. Check available disk space and try again.
ready_to_open: Added “{{title}}”. Open it to read or follow conversion progress.
file_help: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, HTML, CSV, Markdown, or text. Up to 50 MB per file. Scanned PDFs are not supported.
help_hint: Resume setup, watch offline guides, or find keyboard shortcuts.
walkthroughs_body: These illustrated examples run offline. They do not sign you in or send questions. Use Next caption to follow at your own pace.
checklist_body: A few useful first steps. Reopen any of them whenever you need a reminder.
coach_workspace_body: Drag across text in the reader, then choose Ask about this. With the reader focused, Shift + Arrow also selects text. Your selection appears above Chat. Choose a model before sending. Open the conversation menu above Chat to search this document’s chats.
coach_courses: Start with what is due next
coach_courses_body: Connect your school if this page is empty. After syncing, Due soon shows the next seven days. Open a course for Deadlines and the course assistant. Check dates against your school before acting on an AI answer.
shortcuts_body: Use Tab to reach controls and Enter or Space to activate them. Shortcuts work when the relevant view has focus.
school_caption_0: Open Courses from the sidebar. Choose Connect school. No AI account is needed.
school_caption_1: Search for your school or enter its Moodle site URL. Confirm the site before continuing; the app will contact it to find the sign-in method.
school_caption_2: Use your school’s sign-in window and follow its prompts. After syncing, your courses appear here. If login fails, retry in Courses or ask your school for its Moodle URL.
due_caption_0: Open Courses after connecting and syncing your school. Cached work can be read offline, but dates may be out of date.
due_caption_1: Look at Due soon for unsubmitted work in the next seven days. Open an item to see its course.
due_caption_2: Open the course’s Deadlines tab for overdue and later work. Use the reminder control on a deadline to choose a reminder time. Always confirm the school’s date.
agent_caption_0: Open the course related to your question. Its assistant uses that course’s available deadlines and announcements.
agent_caption_1: Choose the chat button at the bottom right. If no AI is connected, open Settings → Providers first. Connecting can send course context to that provider.
agent_caption_2: Ask “What should I prepare before the next deadline?” Check the answer against Deadlines and announcements. Reminders proposed by the assistant need your approval.
selection_caption_0: Add a document or sample in Home or Library, then choose Open. Wait until conversion finishes before selecting text.
selection_caption_1: Drag across one sentence in the reader. Or focus the reader and hold Shift while pressing an arrow key. Choose Ask about this, or press Command + Shift + K.
selection_caption_2: The selection appears above Chat. Choose a connected model, type “Explain this sentence”, and send. Follow any citation back to the source. Without AI, you can still read and practice selecting.
history_caption_0: Open the document you discussed. Conversations currently belong to that document.
history_caption_1: Open the conversation menu above Chat. It lists this document’s past conversations. If there are none, create a conversation after connecting AI.
history_caption_2: Type a word from the conversation title or preview into Search threads. Select a result to reopen it. This search is within the current document, not all coursework.
example_deadline: Lab report · due in two days
example_deadline_question: What should I prepare before the deadline?
recorded_body: Recorded steps from the real app, with an English interface. Choose subtitles in the player. The school and AI responses are test examples, and no real account is used.
record_confirm: Confirm the school before continuing to sign in. This example uses a test school.
step_acquisition: How did you hear about VStudy Pro?
step_acquisition_body: Optional. You can skip this question.
step_privacy_body: Your choice. Both options let you use every study feature.
